findings.claim: The USA refused to recognise Castro’s government
findings.truth: The United States extended recognition to Cuba’s new government on 7 January 1959 and severed diplomatic relations in January 1961. However, the Edexcel P4 content bullet itself refers to a refusal to recognise Castro’s government. Options: follow the specification’s wording, or revise this lesson and its specification-facing framing to distinguish recognition from later diplomatic rupture.
findings.evidence: Edexcel 1HI0 P4 Key topic 2; US Department of State, Office of the Historian, ‘Recognition of the New Government of Cuba’ (7 January 1959), and its Cuba country guide.
findings.ruling: Keep the spec's 'refusal to recognise' as the exam label, state the record: recognised Jan 1959, embargo, relations severed Jan 1961.

findings.claim: Around 500,000 Warsaw Pact troops from the USSR, Poland, Hungary, East Germany and Bulgaria invaded Czechoslovakia.
findings.truth: The invading forces came from the USSR, Poland, Hungary and Bulgaria; East Germany did not send troops into Czechoslovakia.
findings.evidence: US Department of State, Office of the Historian, ‘Czechoslovakia, 1968’, records four participating armies: Soviet, Bulgarian, Polish and Hungarian.

findings.claim: The NPT stopped nuclear states supplying nuclear weapons technology to non-nuclear states.
findings.truth: The NPT prohibits transfer of nuclear weapons or control over them and assistance with acquiring them; it permits peaceful nuclear co-operation subject to safeguards.
findings.evidence: United Nations, Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons, Articles I, III and IV.

findings.claim: The Edexcel period-study paper has a ‘Give Two Things’ source-inference question worth 2 marks.
findings.truth: The current Paper 2P period-study paper begins with a 4-mark consequence task, not a 2-mark source-inference task.
findings.evidence: Pearson Edexcel GCSE History 1HI0 specification, Assessment information; Pearson Paper 2P current sample/assessment materials.

findings.claim: The Edexcel period-study paper has a 4-mark ‘Explain One Cause’ question.
findings.truth: Its 4-mark period-study task is about a consequence, not a cause.
findings.evidence: Pearson Edexcel GCSE History 1HI0 specification, Assessment information; Pearson Paper 2P current sample/assessment materials.

findings.claim: The USSR demanded SDI be abandoned before any new arms-control agreements could be reached.
findings.truth: SDI was a major obstacle at Reykjavík in 1986, but the 1987 INF Treaty was agreed without the United States abandoning it.
findings.evidence: US Department of State, Office of the Historian, documents on the Reykjavík summit and 1987 INF negotiations.

findings.claim: Solidarity won free elections in June 1989.
findings.truth: The June 1989 Polish elections were partly free; Solidarity won all the seats it contested.
findings.evidence: Polish History Museum, account of the June 1989 elections: 161 Sejm seats were freely contested and Solidarity won all contested seats.

findings.claim: The flashcard asks which movement won free elections in June 1989.
findings.truth: The elections were partly free, and Solidarity won all the seats it contested.
findings.evidence: Polish History Museum, account of the June 1989 elections: 161 Sejm seats were freely contested and Solidarity won all contested seats.

findings.claim: Gorbachev demanded that SDI be abandoned as a condition for further arms reduction.
findings.truth: Gorbachev’s demand over SDI blocked agreement at Reykjavík in 1986, but it was not a condition for every later arms-reduction agreement.
findings.evidence: US Department of State, Office of the Historian, Reykjavík summit records; the 1987 INF Treaty followed without abandonment of SDI.

findings.claim: The SDI glossary definition treats abandoning SDI as a condition for further arms reduction.
findings.truth: SDI was a major obstacle at the 1986 Reykjavík talks, not an absolute condition for all later arms reduction.
findings.evidence: US Department of State, Office of the Historian, Reykjavík summit records; the 1987 INF Treaty followed without abandonment of SDI.

findings.claim: The Edexcel period-study paper has a 16-mark ‘How Far Do You Agree’ question.
findings.truth: The period-study paper contains an 8-mark importance task; it does not contain a 16-mark evaluative question in that format.
findings.evidence: Pearson Edexcel GCSE History 1HI0 specification, Assessment information; Pearson Paper 2P current sample/assessment materials.

summary: Checked all eight lessons. Eleven findings were recorded: ten surgical corrections across L5–L8 and one specification-versus-history adjudication in L4.
